previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, bilateral below-knee amputations, and a history of resistant urinary tract infections was admitted for shaking chills and myoclonus. She was found to have bacteremia with coagulase-negative staphylococcus and acute kidney injury, likely due to nephrotoxicity from colistin. Blood pressure dropped transiently in the ED but stabilized with fluids. IV vancomycin was started for bacteremia, and colistin was discontinued. The patient became afebrile, blood cultures cleared, and kidney function stabilized. A new PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic access. She completed a course of IV vancomycin and was discharged on oral vancomycin for C. diff prophylaxis, with medication adjustments for renal function. Follow-up was arranged with her PCP for lab monitoring.
